name: luma-hosted-guest-to-event-attendance

deploy.description: Luma guest on the Notion Singapore calendar (private Luma Calendar API integration, new_or_updated_guest) -> skip invited-only guests and events not in the Luma Managed Events Table -> resolve/create the Event, upsert the Contact (Work Email registration answer becomes Primary Email, new contacts flagged Possible duplicate of name matches) and upsert Event Attendance (Approval Status, Checked In). Sole creator and updater; no Buttondown opt-in. Also fired by luma-manager-email-to-table's backfill.

trigger.authentication_note: Private integration `Luma Calendar API (Unofficial Integration by work.flowers)` (App247901, source work-flowers/zapier-luma-hosted), connection `Notion Singapore Community` holding that calendar's API key. Dennis is not a manager of the calendar, so Zapier's built-in Luma app (OAuth) cannot see it.
trigger.params_note: Empty params = all guests, all statuses, of every event from 2 days ago to 365 days ahead. `approval_statuses` is deliberately unset: invited guests are dropped in code (isInvitedOnly) so that a later registration or check-in still arrives as a new version.
trigger.trigger_note: Polling. The item id is `<guest id>_<approval_status>_<latest check-in | none>`, so a status change or check-in re-fires despite the durable dedupe on the raw id (W6ZE93-VMEWP). Never key a write on it: Notion writes key on the Luma event id, the guest's email and the Event+Contact pair. A guest returning to a state they were already in (approved -> declined -> approved) does not re-fire.

version_pinning_note: @zapier/zapier-durable 0.14.1 (2026-09-29) and @zapier/zapier-sdk 0.115.1 (2026-10-06) were the newest releases at least 24h old at build time. No zod: nothing imports it.

connections_note: notion_wf: work.flowers Notion. typesafe: the `Jev` API-by-Zapier connection holding the TypeSafe key as a Bearer token, called with sdk.fetch (same binding as gmail-attachments-to-drive-by-type and merge-duplicate-contacts).

ai_model.provider: TypeSafe Jev (jev-latest; thresholds checked on jev-1.13.0)
ai_model.used_for: Personal-vs-organisation verdict on an email DOMAIN, to pick a NEW contact's Primary Email. One batched call per new contact whose candidate domains are not yet in the Email Domain Types Table; each domain is judged once, ever. Since 2026-10-21 also: P(same person) for a NEW contact against looser duplicate candidates (not exact-name matches), one pair per call, at most 5 calls; P >= 0.6 flags `Possible duplicate of`, never across two different LinkedIn profiles.
ai_model.why_jev: A typed yes/no probability over a short string fits Jev's question types; Dennis did not want a hard-coded personal-domain list (2026-10-15). Offline run over all 208 real domains: every consumer provider >= 0.38, every organisation <= 0.29 (README).
ai_model.cost: 1 Zapier task per Jev call plus ~$0.0001 TypeSafe tokens; cached domains (gmail.com etc.) cost nothing. Duplicate check: 1 Zapier task per Jev call, usually 0-2 per new contact, max 5.
ai_model.duplicate_flag_threshold: P(same person) >= 0.6. Offline 2026-10-21 over 187 real candidate pairs: duplicates >= 0.80, different people <= 0.46 (README 'Possible-duplicate flags').
